title: SanDisk portable SSD not detected
shortDescription: Computer doesn't see the portable SSD.
fullDescription:
SanDisk Extreme Pro and portable SSDs occasionally fail to enumerate due to the well-known SD/Extreme firmware bug, bad USB-C cable, or power delivery issues.

Firmware updates addressed a major failure wave in 2023 – check version first.

fixSteps.title: Firmware check
fixSteps.instruction: Install SanDisk Dashboard / Western Digital Dashboard and update firmware.

fixSteps.title: Use quality USB-C cable
fixSteps.instruction: Use a certified USB-C 10 Gbps cable, not a charge-only cable.

fixSteps.title: Claim warranty
fixSteps.instruction: Many affected Extreme/Extreme Pro are eligible for warranty replacement.

whenToCallPro: Critical data on failed Extreme series – data recovery, then RMA.
videoSearchQuery: SanDisk Extreme SSD not recognized fix

faq.q: Is my drive in the affected batch?
faq.a: Pre-firmware-update Extreme Pro V2 with certain controllers – check SanDisk advisory.

title: TRIM not passing through to SanDisk SSD
shortDescription: OS can't send TRIM commands to the SSD.
fullDescription: TRIM keeps SSDs fast by telling them which blocks are freed. External enclosures, USB bridges, or RAID controllers may block TRIM, leading to performance degradation over time.

fixSteps.title: Check TRIM status
fixSteps.instruction: Windows: 'fsutil behavior query DisableDeleteNotify'. macOS: system_profiler SPSerialATADataType.

fixSteps.title: Enable TRIM
fixSteps.instruction: Windows: 'fsutil behavior set DisableDeleteNotify 0'. macOS: trimforce enable.

fixSteps.title: Swap enclosure
fixSteps.instruction: If USB bridge blocks TRIM, use a UASP-capable enclosure.

faq.a: No – it only hints the SSD which blocks are unused.

title: SanDisk SSD throttling under sustained load
shortDescription: Sustained writes drop far below advertised speeds.
fullDescription: Portable SSDs throttle to protect controller and NAND from thermal damage. The Extreme series gets hot quickly due to small aluminum housing. SLC cache exhaustion also causes sharp speed drops.
symptoms: Speed drops from 1000 MB/s to ~300 MB/s

fixSteps.title: Improve cooling
fixSteps.instruction: Place on a metal surface or use a small fan during long transfers.

fixSteps.title: Break up writes
fixSteps.instruction: Pause between large batches to let SLC cache clear.

fixSteps.title: Use USB 3.2 Gen 2
fixSteps.instruction: Connect to a 10 Gbps port for full throughput.

faq.a: No – it protects the drive but reduces speed.

title: SanDisk SSD needs firmware update
fullDescription: SanDisk released critical firmware updates for the Extreme / Extreme Pro Portable SSD line after widespread data loss reports in 2023. Updating is strongly recommended.

fixSteps.title: Back up data
fixSteps.instruction: Back up to another drive BEFORE firmware update.

fixSteps.title: Verify version
fixSteps.instruction: After update confirm firmware version reported in dashboard.

affectedModels: SanDisk Extreme Pro Portable SSD V2
whenToCallPro: If firmware update bricks drive, contact SanDisk support.

faq.a: Yes, but always back up data first.

title: SanDisk SSD SMART critical warning
shortDescription: SMART attributes indicate critical wear or failure.
fullDescription: Dashboard flagged a critical SMART attribute such as Media Wearout, Available Spare, or Uncorrectable Errors. Back up immediately and plan replacement.

fixSteps.title: Check SMART attributes
fixSteps.instruction: Note attribute IDs that tripped to diagnose cause.

fixSteps.title: Plan replacement
fixSteps.instruction: Don't use drive for new data – RMA if in warranty.

whenToCallPro: If drive fails before full backup complete.

faq.a: Not for important data – likely to fail soon.

title: SanDisk SSD over-temperature
shortDescription: SSD hits thermal limit and throttles or disconnects.
fullDescription: Portable SSD aluminum housings absorb heat fast. Sustained writes or hot environments push controller temps past 70-80°C, triggering throttle or emergency shutdown.

fixSteps.title: Improve airflow
fixSteps.instruction: Place on metal stand, avoid fabric surfaces.

fixSteps.title: Split large jobs
fixSteps.instruction: Break backups into smaller chunks with rest periods.

faq.a: Below 70°C under load; above that throttle activates.

title: SanDisk SSD reporting bad blocks
shortDescription: NAND blocks failing and being remapped.
fullDescription: Every SSD retires worn blocks; normal at low rate. Rising bad block count indicates wear-out nearing end of life. Back up and consider replacement.
symptoms: Dashboard reports bad block count rising

fixSteps.title: Back up now
fixSteps.instruction: Copy data to a fresh drive.

fixSteps.title: Check TBW vs rating
fixSteps.instruction: If near or past rated TBW, normal wear-out – replace.

fixSteps.title: RMA if premature
fixSteps.instruction: If low host writes but many bad blocks, RMA.

faq.a: A few yes; rapidly growing count is not.

title: SanDisk SSD in read-only mode
shortDescription: Drive became read-only due to wear-out protection.
fullDescription: When NAND reaches end of life, SanDisk drives may enter read-only mode to preserve data. This is terminal – data can be copied off but no further writes possible.

fixSteps.title: Back up data
fixSteps.instruction: Copy everything off immediately – read-only is usually terminal.

fixSteps.title: Replace drive
fixSteps.instruction: SSD at end of life – retire.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed – drive is effectively dead.

title: SanDisk SSD I/O errors
fullDescription: I/O errors on an SSD point to firmware bugs, USB bridge problems, or failing NAND. Back up before further troubleshooting.

fixSteps.title: Cable and port swap
fixSteps.instruction: Try new USB-C cable and different port.

affectedModels: SanDisk Extreme Pro Portable SSD V2

faq.a: Similar symptom, different causes – SSDs fail suddenly.

title: SanDisk SSD SecureAccess locked
shortDescription: Drive shows only the SecureAccess vault app.
fullDescription: SanDisk SecureAccess creates an encrypted vault on the drive. Without the password the vault contents cannot be accessed.

fixSteps.title: Reset = data loss
fixSteps.instruction: Forgotten password = data unrecoverable; only option is to delete vault and lose contents.

whenToCallPro: Professional recovery unlikely to help with AES-256 encryption.

faq.a: No – SanDisk cannot recover the password.
